entry.title: You Are In The Bike Lane Richmond, October 29

author.name: You Are In The Bike Lane Richmond

entry.content:
From You Are In The Bike Lane Richmond



The Mayo Bridge that connects Manchester to Shockoe Bottom is old and crumbling, so the city is building a replacement bridge directly next to the current one. The link to the survey to give your feedback on the proposed design is in my bio, and you have between now and this Sunday, November 1st, to fill it out.

This is our best opportunity yet to finally get real barrier-protected bike lanes on a bridge here in Richmond. Unfortunately, the current proposal only separates cyclists from busy car traffic using 3-inch bumps. These bumps won't stop drivers from illegally parking or driving in the bike lanes. We know unprotected bike lanes cause delays for emergency services and force cyclists to merge into dangerous car traffic to get around cars.

Thankfully, there's an alternative design that's been popping up across the U.S. that uses barrier-protected bike lanes to give emergency services a way to bypass car traffic. These are called Safety Lanes because they've been proven to improve response times for emergency vehicles while also improving safety for cyclists and pedestrians. This model would be easy for VDOT to adopt because guidelines for emergency vehicles using bike lanes already exist in a design guide Richmond and VDOT already reference.

So fill out the Mayo Bridge Public Survey from the link in my bio, say no to the current proposal that uses small mountable bumps, and ask for safety lanes, barrier-protected double-wide bike lanes that meet the community's safety needs while improving emergency response times.
